summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS lymphoma, diabetes insipidus, and histiocytosis X was admitted for his third cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He presented in stable condition, reporting mild right ear fullness but no other symptoms. He tolerated the methotrexate infusion well without acute side effects. IV fluids with sodium bicarbonate were administered to support methotrexate clearance, and leucovorin rescue was continued. Methotrexate levels decreased appropriately, reaching 0.04 by discharge. Hyponatremia developed during treatment, with serum sodium dropping to 130, prompting a one-time hold of DDAVP; sodium stabilized at 131. Dexamethasone was tapered to 2 mg daily per protocol. The patient remained seizure-free on levetiracetam and normotensive on lisinopril. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor electrolytes and continue home medications.
